summary: Bidirectional alignment fails after a full matrix walk. The verifier requires reject detail text containing "negative" and a bin substring src.cli that the solver-visible contract does not state; it also forces one journal line per valid event while the contract says each watermark advance appends. Material contract rules are untested: watermark-triggered closes, --reset-output preservation of in-flight sessions, and unknown-flag non-mutation of side outputs.

evidence.observation: Two paragraphs: repair the Python sessionizer; binding contract at /app/sessions/docs/session-contract.md; CLI /app/sessions/bin/run-sessions; unknown flags fail before journal or output touch; --input tie-break; --feed file order; --reset-output wipes side files not journal or in-flight sessions; event-time tenant+user half-open sessions; knobs in processor.json; persist watermark.journal and open-session state; idempotent digests; empty input; rejects.jsonl; leave warehouse alone.

Binding CLI, schemas, gap/duration, watermark formula and per-event decision order, late-but-allowed vs TOO_LATE, watermark-triggered closes (last+gap <= W), journal seq, restart snapshot, --reset-output must not clear journal or open-session state, reject record with detail as a short reason, forbidden language rewrite.
Incident notes with symptom times (85000 after 100000, 1000ms straggler, mixed tenants, reset wiping journal, seq stuck at 1). Referenced by instruction.md as shift notes.
Captured log under the instruction-named logs directory; records misclassification and journal rewrite symptoms. Not a schema/CLI contract.
Public operator wrapper execs python3 -m src.cli. Instruction requires a Python processor and this CLI path; it does not name the src.cli module.
Public knobs session_gap_ms=30000, allowed_lateness_ms=10000, max_session_duration_ms=3600000 match the contract example.
Operator CLI surface: --input/--feed/--reset-output/--empty-check. Used only to interpret documented flags, not as a graded implementation recipe.

36 pytest behaviors: unknown-flag/empty/gap/tenant/journal/late/reject/idempotent/restart/config/holdout/tie-break/feed-order/reset/schema/warehouse/bin. Autouse restores processor.json and clears runtime files.

Holdouts feed_late, feed_order, lateness_probe, tie_break, holdout_sessions, and zero-byte empty.jsonl. feed_late is the late-allowed/too-late scenario; holdout_sessions includes a bob key that would watermark-close under the contract but is never asserted.
Public five-event sample used for gap [1000,35000), tenant split, event_count, journal seq length 5, and idempotent digests.
Classification labels only (F2P vs P2P). Not used as coverage rationale.
Every tested behavior must be discoverable; every stated requirement must be tested; no phantom specs; schemas/paths named in instruction or a referenced contract.
Material goals in instruction.md; docs may hold schema/CLI/protocol; no repair map or fixture-specific hidden values; implementation diagnosis only when evidence-backed and natural to the handoff.

PASS needs empty BLOCKING_FINDING_IDS plus a complete exhaustive walk. BLOCKER/HIGH always block; MEDIUM blocks when it can change pass/fail, observable correctness, safety, or a documented public interface.

findings.why_it_matters: The contract requires a REJECT_MALFORMED record with a short reason. The test requires the substring "negative" in detail. A correct reject of event_time_ms < 0 that says "event_time_ms must be >= 0" fails grading. That can change solver pass/fail.
findings.minimal_remediation: Assert code REJECT_MALFORMED and that the negative-time line is not treated as late; drop the detail-substring canary, or state the required detail token in the public contract.
findings.regression_risk: Low if the behavioral reject/not-late check remains.

findings.why_it_matters: The contract requires that after each watermark update, every open session with last_event_time_ms + session_gap_ms <= W is closed. Tests only assert same-key arrival gap closes. Holdout bob (h4 at 15000) would close at 45000 once W reaches 70000 after h5, but no test reads bob. A processor that never watermark-closes idle keys can still pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add a behavioral assert that an idle other-key session closes when the watermark passes last+gap, using a hidden variation of the published rule.
findings.regression_risk: Low; tightens an already-published close rule.

findings.why_it_matters: The contract says each watermark advance appends a journal line and seq increases per append. sample_basic has five valid events but only three max_observed increases (1000, 5000, 40000). The test requires seqs == 1..n and len==5, i.e. one line per observation including unchanged watermarks. Two competent readings exist; only the per-observation reading passes.
findings.minimal_remediation: State in the contract whether a journal line is written for every successfully parsed event or only when watermark_ms changes, then match the seq-length assert to that rule.
findings.regression_risk: Medium if existing journal tests assume five lines; keep prefix/nondecreasing checks either way.

findings.why_it_matters: Instruction requires repairing the existing Python processor and not moving session logic to another language. The test also requires the bin text to contain src.cli. A Python entry that still drives /app/sessions/bin/run-sessions but uses a different module path fails. That is an implementation name, not a published interface, and it changes pass/fail.
findings.minimal_remediation: Keep a python3 (or equivalent CPython) launch check on the public bin; drop the src.cli substring unless that module is declared as a stable public interface.
findings.regression_risk: Low if the language/CLI path requirement remains.

findings.why_it_matters: Instruction and contract say --reset-output may truncate side files and must not clear the watermark journal or in-flight open-session state. The reset test checks journal bytes and emptied sessions/late after --empty-check; it never reads open_sessions.json. Wiping in-flight keys on reset still passes. That is a documented public interface and restart-safety requirement.
findings.minimal_remediation: After a run that leaves open sessions, invoke --reset-output and assert open_sessions.json identity/event_ids are unchanged while side JSONL files are truncated.

findings.why_it_matters: Unknown flags must fail with exit 2 before mutating journal, open-session state, or outputs. Tests assert exit 2 and journal non-creation/non-clearing only. Creating or truncating sessions.jsonl/late.jsonl/rejects.jsonl (or open_sessions.json) on an unknown flag still passes, so the documented pre-mutation barrier is only half-graded.
findings.minimal_remediation: On unknown flags, also assert side outputs and open-session state are not created or altered (including --reset-output combined with an unknown flag).

findings.why_it_matters: f3 at 85000 after a 100000 anchor joins the open session whether it is classified late-but-allowed or wrongly treated as on-time; last_event_time_ms is not checked. Too-late f4 is separately graded. Advisory: the late-but-allowed last-event update rule is not uniquely observed.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: assert last_event_time_ms stays 100000 after f3, or use a fixture where on-time gap-close would diverge from late-but-allowed join.

findings.why_it_matters: Contract says continue with later lines after a reject, do not emit duplicate closes, journal raw negative watermarks while comparisons use max(0,W), and --reset-output truncates rejects.jsonl. None of those are asserted. Primary reject/late/gap paths exist, so these are sibling edges rather than missing work-request goals.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional asserts: a valid line after malformed JSON is processed; closed (tenant,user,start,end) pairs are unique; a first observation below allowed_lateness journals a negative watermark_ms; reset truncates rejects.

findings.why_it_matters: Unknown flags must exit 2. Omitting --input/--feed/--empty-check is not named as an unknown flag, but the test grades empty argv as exit 2 with no journal. A usage-error exit 1 would fail. Advisory: most CLIs use 2 for usage, so this is unlikely to mislead a fair solve.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: say that a missing source is a usage error with the same exit 2 and pre-mutation barrier as unknown flags.

findings.why_it_matters: Leave-warehouse-alone is graded by SHA-256 after a run. The extra >=10000 line floor is a private cardinality on inherited data. The contract-file test greps one formula string, which is a brittle proxy for not rewriting the doc. Neither changes a correct leave-alone/Python repair if the inherited dump and contract remain.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: keep warehouse untouched-hash only; keep contract path presence without a formula substring.

findings.why_it_matters: --input must tie-break equal event times by (tenant_id, user_id, event_id). The permutation test only proves some file-order-independent order. On this fixture, sorting by user_id or by event_id both yield t0,t1,t2. A correct full-key sort still passes.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional holdout where user_id order and event_id order disagree.

findings.why_it_matters: On-call notes and the bounce log list incident symptoms (including times and event ids that match the hidden late feed). They do not name modules/functions. That is realistic current-state evidence more than a second prompt; material goals remain in instruction.md plus the contract. Advisory leakage only.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional: keep symptoms qualitative in oncall.md and let the public sample fixtures carry concrete times, or use incident times that are not identical to hidden holdout ids.
findings.regression_risk: Low; do not strip current-state evidence entirely.

do_not_change: Published event-time gap, lateness formula, tenant key, and --feed file-order rules already covered by F2P tests
Unknown-flag exit 2 plus journal non-mutation asserts
Hidden holdout files as examples; requirements must remain public
next_gate: Q2 Verifier Coverage Repairer for untested watermark-close/reset-open/unknown-flag output barriers and the reject-detail/src.cli phantoms; Q3 Spec Ambiguity Repairer for journal append cadence; Q1 only if those rules are added to the solver-visible contract. Then a new Q4 packet on the repaired task commit.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.requirement: Repair the existing Python processor; drive work through /app/sessions/bin/run-sessions; do not move session logic to another language.
Unknown flags exit 2 before mutating journal, open-session state, or outputs.
--input is a batch ordered by event_time_ms then (tenant_id, user_id, event_id).
--feed processes strictly in file order so out-of-order event times are preserved.
--reset-output truncates side JSONL files and must not clear the watermark journal or in-flight sessions.
Empty input / --empty-check leaves sessions.jsonl and late.jsonl empty and does not advance the watermark journal.
Sessions are event-time keyed by (tenant_id, user_id) and must not merge equal user ids across tenants.
On-time gap closes use event_time_ms and emit half-open [start_ms, end_ms) with end = last + gap.
If accepting an event would exceed max_session_duration_ms, close at start + max duration then open a new session if the event is otherwise acceptable.
watermark_ms = max_observed_event_time_ms - allowed_lateness_ms; undefined until the first valid observation; non-decreasing across observations and restarts.
After updating W, close every open session where last_event_time_ms + session_gap_ms <= W.
Late-but-allowed events join the open session; too-late events go to late.jsonl with reason TOO_LATE and the comparison watermark.
Malformed JSON and illegal fields fail closed into rejects.jsonl as REJECT_MALFORMED and are not late.
Persist watermark.journal as JSONL with seq starting at 1, increasing per append, prefix-stable across runs, never stepping backward.
Reload journal and open-session state across restarts so in-flight sessions and seq continue and the watermark never steps backward.
From a clean journal, a second identical run reproduces the same SHA-256 digests for sessions.jsonl and late.jsonl.
Honor /app/sessions/config/processor.json; changing gap, lateness, or max duration changes behavior.
Closed session records include tenant_id, user_id, start_ms, end_ms, event_ids, event_count==len(event_ids); late records include watermark_ms and TOO_LATE.
Leave /app/sessions/warehouse (production click dump) alone.
Treat session-contract.md as binding; do not throw away the journal protocol or rewrite the contract to excuse incorrect behavior.

PHANTOM_TEST_CONTRACTS.enforced: exactly one journal line per valid sample_basic event (len==5)
PHANTOM_TEST_CONTRACTS.solver_visible: each watermark advance appends; seq +1 per append; non-decreasing watermark_ms

REQ-CLI-UNKNOWN non-mutation of side outputs and open-session state
Continue processing later lines after a malformed reject
Journal records raw negative watermark_ms; lateness comparisons use max(0, W)
Crash-consistent snapshot replace / whole-line journal appends
Late-but-allowed updates last_event_time_ms only when the late event_time is greater

AMBIGUITIES.interpretation_a: Write a journal line for every successfully parsed event, including unchanged watermark_ms
AMBIGUITIES.interpretation_b: Write a journal line only when watermark_ms increases
AMBIGUITIES.grading: test_f2p_journal_seq_starts_at_one accepts only A (len==5 on sample_basic)

AMBIGUITIES.interpretation_a: Missing --input/--feed/--empty-check is a usage error with exit 2
AMBIGUITIES.interpretation_b: Missing source is a different error (exit 1) or implicit empty-check

DELEGATED_CONTRACT_CHECK.notes/oncall.md: LEGITIMATE incident notes with some fixture-like times; not the source of graded schemas

F2P_P2P_WALK.f2p: Unknown-flag journal mutation, empty/zero input, gap/tenant/journal/late/idempotent/restart/config-gap/holdout/feed-order/reset/watermark formula are owned as fail-to-pass against the defective starter.
F2P_P2P_WALK.p2p: Warehouse leave-alone, bin/contract presence, python launch, config keys, output path parents, malformed JSON reject, negative-time reject, late-allowed join, max-duration close, and tie-break stability are labeled preservation. Negative-time P2P is coupled to starter detail spelling (Q4-B01). Late-allowed P2P does not uniquely distinguish on-time join (Q4-A01). No circular oracle: tests drive run-sessions and parse outputs.
F2P_P2P_WALK.bypass_risk: src.cli and negative-detail greps can be satisfied without correct session semantics; warehouse 10k is inherited size not processor behavior.

OUTPUT_INTERFACES_WALK.open_sessions.json: tenant split and restart extend; not reset-output preservation
